items.text: Since the Night Shift Update you've been busy reporting bugs to us, thank you for that! Today we have a small patch with fixes.

In Hightower, baggage falling from the upper floor to the ground floor could drop through conveyor belts. Collision detection is now much more precise, so it should run stable. If a suitcase still slips through, please let us know.
Baggage on the first or last meter of a Straight (3m) could get sucked into a sorter next to it. That doesn't happen anymore.
When leaving your home, you couldn't select all 10 job save slots. All of them are available now.
Sorters on upper levels didn't work properly in some cases, and the baggage piled up in front of them. This is now fixed.
We fixed a case where you could get stuck in the tutorial.
The book DLC wasn't displayed properly on the Steam Deck, it works now.
You've sent us lots of great screenshots again, thank you! Today's selection comes from ROI801, Kaonashi and BomboloReDeRoma from our Discord server!
With you can activate screenshot mode in the game! :)
As always, thank you for all your feedback! Every report from the game reaches us, and many of the fixes in this patch go straight back to your reports. 😎
And always remember: airport operations tolerate no negligence!
Stable regards,
Günther!
Three River Games (3RG)

This is Günther Gewinn speaking. My airports never sleep, and as of today neither do you: as Managing Director, it is my honor to announce Version 1.1 of our game, the Night Shift Update! To mark the occasion, I've brought you a glimpse from Starville, my first airport where you can work the night shift:
In Starville, your baggage arrives from two inputs at once. As soon as you have completed Hall 1, you can take the job in my office, you don't need to have played through Hamville first.

Different rules apply on the night shift, but I expect the same diligence in your workflow. Denise, for example, says she can't get the hang of shift work at all so far, but somehow the decorating still works out. Anyway, here's the short version:
Night bonus: you earn $0.50 extra salary for every valid piece of baggage when you complete the job.
Shop prices are 10% higher at night. Horst says he needs the money "to motivate his biceps".
Unlocking gates costs 50% more during night shifts.

You are not entirely alone at night. I hired Walter Wachsam, for instance (great guy!). Walter simply has a whole lot of experience in being watchful, and at the start of your first shift he tells you how this whole working at night thing goes. He's basically like Ute, just not as cheerful, but more watchful! You'll also meet this cat in every night shift airport, I don't really know how she keeps getting in here. In any case, you can pet Kosmo. You should pet Kosmo!

notes.title: You can use all five in every job, not only at night

items.text: Elevator: lifts baggage 2m upward, accident-free (see the GIF above).
Straight (3m): a fast 3m conveyor belt. It can also pick up parcels from Horst in the parcel zone.
Passage (3m): a high, 5m wide bridge with a 3m wide passage underneath.
Storage (x25): has 25 storage spots instead of only 10 like the previous storage unit.
Counter: counts +1 every time something is pushed through, and records that number for today and for all time.

For all of you who have long since collected more money than you can spend (I do understand, after all you earn so well working here), there is now a safe under the stairs in your home that you can use to pay into your retirement savings. For every deposit into your retirement savings, you get a starting bonus from me whenever you begin a new job. Simply because I'm especially fond of employees who won't be a burden on the company in old age. It's just important to look after yourself!

notes.title: 🔬 New Skill: Research and More Room for New Jobs 🔬

items.text: To do justice to your endless motivation to work, you can now invest your leftover skill points into the "Research" skill without any limit. For every point in Research, you start a new job with + 1 UP and can get your automation running faster. On top of that, there are now 5 more save slots for starting new jobs, so 10 in total. It would be a shame if you ever ran out of work!

A quick reminder of how this works: before a new job starts, you sit down with me for the Situation Briefing. That's where you decide under which conditions you work this job: benefits make the work easier for you, burdens make it harder. Each of them counts points toward the Situation, and only once the situation is Balanced do I clear the job. So anyone treating themselves to a benefit takes on a burden in the same breath.

notes.title: As of today you have four new options

items.text: Benefit Ascent: speed of bridges, elevators and small corners + 50%.
Benefit Industry 2.0: every purchased sorter starts with one speed upgrade.
Burden Economic Crisis: shop prices + 20%.
Burden 60th Birthday: you cannot throw anymore. Your arms aren't what they used to be.

So you don't forget what you signed up for, every job now has a Benefits and Burdens TV that lists all active modifiers with icon, name, balance and effect. Every job also has a TV with your baggage statistics: the current day, how much baggage you have handled correctly and wrongly in this job, and your accuracy.

You wish to take on even more night shifts? As Managing Director, I like to hear that. Also available today is the Night Shift DLC: three more airports with over 10 hours of additional playtime, all running under the same night shift rules. Once the DLC is installed, you can take the three new jobs in my office.
Newfield: two baggage inputs on different levels. The new elevator could be just the right thing here.
Hightower: a narrow, very tall hall where you work on two floors. A door on the ground floor takes you to the upper level, and the baggage gets back down all by itself: through gravity.
Meadowvale: two separate halls for experts, connected only at the gates. Both halls have every output, so you should run all checks in both halls.
UP Sounds can now be muted in the audio settings, right below XP Sounds.

If you own the Executive Chair, the notice in my office now disappears after 5 seconds instead of 15. That long, it used to stay on top of the interface and cover your display while you were already talking to me.
Several performance improvements, especially for large airports with many buildings and conveyor belts.
The level 4 speed upgrade of the Sorter (Tag) cost $2,000. That was too much, it is now $1,200.
The Lost & Found delivery quest in the tutorial could fail to complete in rare cases, which left the tutorial stuck.
You could place a building inside yourself and end up outside of the level. Entertaining as it was, this is now fixed.
Parcels in a baggage cart were counted as baggage, snapped into place and showed "+1" and "-1" pop-ups.
Baggage you stored in your backpack from a baggage cart still counted as part of that cart.
Sorters could still process baggage that was already in your backpack.
The scale did not reset when you stored the baggage on it in your backpack.
Sorters and storage units placed next to each other could hand over baggage even when they stood at different heights.
The substance sniffer ignored "Flip" right after being built, so the direction reset on every load.
Thanks for reading, and have fun on the night shift! 🌙🧳
And always remember: airport operations tolerate no negligence, not even at night (Walter is watchful)!
Stable regards,
Günther!
Three River Games (3RG)

releases.displayName: The Night Shift Update arrives October 1

items.text: What a summer! Since the release in May you have left us almost 120 reviews, 90% of them positive, plus countless ideas and bug reports on Steam and Discord. Thank you for that, it keeps us going. Today we have an announcement for you: in just under 30 days, on October 1, the Night Shift Update arrives, and with it the Night Shift DLC. The DLC's Steam page is live as of now. If you like what you see, add it to your wishlist, we can't wait to finally show you what we have been working on these past months! 🌙

Some airports have a night shift. And airports with a night shift have two baggage inputs. More suitcases, more responsibility, but also more pay: for the unusual working hours, every valid piece of baggage earns you a night bonus.

You won't be entirely on your own. Walter Wachsam, the night watchman, supports you with valuable tips. Well, maybe they are not that valuable. But at least he is there. And for morale you have your cat Kosmo. Sure, she sleeps most of the time. But not always. Meow!
The Night Shift Update is free for everyone: October 1

With the Night Shift Update, Starville arrives on October 1, your first airport with two baggage inputs and a night bonus, plus new building parts, new modifiers, different working hours, and of course Walter and Kosmo. Once you have completed Hall 1 you can switch straight to Starville, no need to play through to Schinkenheim first. And the new building parts and modifiers are not just for the night: you can use them in every job, including the existing airports.

And for all of you who have long collected more money and skill points than you can spend: with the Night Shift Update you can put both into permanent upgrades that give you a head start every time you take on a job at a new airport. More on that in the patch notes for the update.
The Night Shift DLC

Up for more night shifts? That's what the DLC is for: three more airports in the night shift, each with its own layout and its own challenges. Together we expect over 10 hours of additional playtime, for the price of a large cappuccino. ☕
At a glance

notes.title: Night Shift Update, free for everyone, October 1

items.text: Starville, your first airport with two baggage inputs and a night bonus
New building parts and modifiers, usable in every job
Walter Wachsam and Kosmo the cat
Permanent upgrades for surplus money and skill points
Three more airports in the night shift, each with its own layout
Over 10 hours of additional playtime

It's been about four weeks since our release on May 28, and in that time over 7,000 of you have played our game on Steam, at 95% positive reviews. That's fantastic, and we want to thank every single one of you for it! 🎉❤️
Right now we're working on bringing our game to PS5 and Xbox, and in parallel we keep fixing bugs and issues on PC.

We've also decided to give all your suggestions, ideas and wishes for how we could expand our game a place of their own. That's why, before the end of the year, there will be a first content DLC that picks up where the current jobs end.
You can look forward to the details. A more detailed roadmap, will follow as soon as we're done with the porting! :)
And of course there's a new patch for you today, too. Here are the highlights:
Every 30 minutes you spend playing, you'll find one of the six new trading cards. Trade them or craft badges from them to unlock emoticons or backgrounds for your Steam profile. 😎

Jumbo baggage thrown straight into an automat with a launcher had a problem: the suitcase unfortunately kept its momentum when the automat spat it back out. In rare cases this caused the issue you can see in the GIF below, and it's now fixed, despite its entertainment value:

When building, you could rotate a piece in your hand with and or the mouse wheel. In the key bindings, though, both rotate directions only showed the mouse wheel and couldn't be changed, so all of you who had moved your movement onto / ended up rotating things in your hand while walking. As a fix, for rotating pieces left and right we now only show the keyboard binding to remap, and no longer the mouse wheel. The mouse wheel still works, of course, but can no longer be reassigned. That lets everyone whose was used both for walking and for rotating suitcases tidy up their key bindings.

We've kept working hard on the game and have a new patch for you today. Here are the highlights:
At the button on the wall that you use to start your shift, you can now buy upgrades with to increase the speed at which baggage comes in. This upgrade has two levels:
Level 1: $5,000 and 100 UP, baggage now appears every 4s instead of every 5s.

Throwing now sits on its own key that you can configure, and is no longer hard-wired to the left mouse button or . This came from your feedback, because some of you use special keyboards and need the E key to move around. :)

notes.title: Book DLC integrated into the game

items.text: The Book DLC now sits in your room as an interactive 3D object and can also be opened in-game via the pause menu, for everyone who doesn't want to read a separate PDF.
Some of you don't enjoy our jokes in the long run :( So there's now a slider to fade their volume down. You can also pick between different variants of the XP sounds, or turn them off completely.

The splitter didn't distribute correctly in certain cases when it was flipped with . That works again now!

We kept gathering your feedback attentively over the weekend and have brought you the next patch right away today.
Time and again we got feedback that, for some sorters, the available configurations of inputs and outputs aren't enough to build with them intuitively or in a space-saving way.

That's why it's now possible to cycle through all possible combinations on every sorter with . We got this feedback especially about the airport sorters, because unfortunately it was cumbersome so far to switch them through nicely in a row. Now that works! :)
New app in the tablet: Errors

Time and again we got feedback that it isn't entirely clear why baggage sometimes wasn't handed over correctly, and that many of you wish you could better understand what actually goes wrong there. That's why you'll now find an app in the tablet where all the facts about every error you newly make from this version on can be looked up and traced.
This also helps us going forward to pin down exactly whether there's still a bug somewhere, or whether someone simply assigned a suitcase incorrectly.
Here's an example in which a suitcase that's actually too heavy was mistakenly thrown into the exit for invalid stickers.

At the start of the game, after you've placed the substance sniffer, there's the quest to find a suitcase with an illegal substance and process it "correctly". That means bringing it either to the police or to Risky-Rolf. The problem is that we kept observing players trip over the fact that, at this point, it isn't yet really clear that these suitcases that go to the police also have to be scanned red. The issue then is that if the suitcase is sent away unscanned, the quest doesn't count as completed, and it can take unexpectedly long until a new suitcase with illegal substances randomly appears. To smooth this out, a new suitcase with illegal substances now keeps appearing until the quest has been completed correctly, so that we don't build up too much frustration here and lose players this early in the game.

We fixed an issue where no new building parts could be placed on unexpected spots on the grid after you had cleared away junk there. We heard about this from you again and again, and thanks to all the feedback and your logs we could finally trace it back to the junk not really being gone until you restarted the game.

There was an issue where the airport sorter initially had the value "---", but this value was evaluated by the sorter as FRA and also showed FRA after reloading. This led to some ugly errors. We've fixed it so that you can now actually set "---", and that means, as expected, that there is NO filtering.

We've also improved the preview of the airport sorter (and some other sorters too) in build mode, so that you can now always read on the floor what's actually selected. For example, you can now read which airports you've set; previously only FRA was ever shown, no matter what was set. Here's an impression from the game:

In Farmbrook we got feedback a few times that building parts or pieces of baggage could disappear at the raised spots in the floor. We've made the floor thicker at these spots now, so this problem should no longer occur.
The home upgrades in the bedroom mistakenly gave both more XP and UP; that wasn't intended. They now only give an XP bonus, exactly as the description states.
It's no longer possible to rotate the camera in the background while the pause menu is open.
There were cases where the TV in the hallway in Terminal 1, which teases the new jobs, unexpectedly was visible through the door.
The door to Günther Gewinn in Hall 1 couldn't be closed all that easily, because an invisible object was in the way.
The green checkmark on the automatic scanner for valid suitcases was rotated the wrong way around.

On the texture of the sorter for overweight suitcases, the weight symbols were rotated the wrong way around.: Twitch drops until tonight, 23:59 UTC: Until tonight (for roughly 12 more hours after this patch) you still have the chance to grab the Twitch drops for our game. Many thanks to all the streamers and viewers who took part and had fun with it!: We're optimistic that the drops will return one day! 😎: Here's the link for everyone who wants to earn a last-minute drop: https://www.twitch.tv/directory/category/airport-baggage-simulator?filter=drops

Three River Games (3RG)
We've kept gathering your feedback attentively and have brought you our first slightly bigger patch since release today. Here are the details:

There's now a new upgrade on the baggage cart that you can unlock via the upgrade menu (look at the baggage cart and press \). Once you buy this upgrade, you'll have a new fully automatic storage module right next to the baggage cart. It comes with a few neat features:

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45764717/4c6db1b94876efc060a3edcebe205b96e084e20b.gif"]- It can load the baggage cart automatically and will only throw in suitcases that match the active flight at the gate.
It has a handy connection for your conveyor belt automation that works more reliably than loading the baggage carts with the thrower (even if that does look cool).
With 12 slots for suitcases it holds more than the regular storage.
It's placed outside the existing build grid, which means it's automatically compatible with your existing setups.

It unloads about 3 suitcases per second into the baggage cart, as many as will fit (roughly up to 10, depending on which baggage types are currently around). That means even when your gate is already fully automated, you can fairly easily get rid of surplus suitcases that have piled up over time.: This upgrade costs you $800 and 16 UP wrenches. We hope it helps you build a satisfying connection from your automation to the baggage carts and clear out your old surplus suitcases.

We've increased the number of slots that suitcases automatically snap to when you throw them into the baggage cart from 6 to 9. We've also made the box you have to throw into, so the suitcases snap to a fixed position in the baggage cart, bigger. That means you don't have to aim quite as precisely and it's easier to load more than 6 suitcases into the cart.

Many of you have reached out to us because it annoys you that, once the backpack is unlocked, other building parts keep getting picked up accidentally while you're collecting suitcases. That's why there's now a new setting that lets you define more precisely how this should behave. There are three options:
1) All building parts can be quickly collected with \
2) All building parts except storage and tables can be quickly collected with \
3) No building parts can be quickly collected with \
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45764717/3dcc556149e5bc569757f39170bd516cd8c1a668.png"]

We hope this lets everyone adjust the behavior so it fits their play style. Option 2 is the new default after you install the update. The reason is that we got an especially large amount of feedback about people accidentally collecting tables or their entire fully packed storage with \ when they really only wanted to grab a single suitcase.
Many of you wished that we would, first, improve how you can tell what's inside parcels and, second, give you a way to see which upgrades the various building parts already have.
For the upgrades, we've expanded the little text you've always seen when looking at building parts. Here's an impression:
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45764717/8239fb1bebbb53963b3c13603d2e676de770273b.png"]

For parcels, we've adjusted things so that you also see this label when looking at a parcel lying on the floor, and we've added a nice sticker on top that contains the same information again. Here's an impression of that as well:
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45764717/4904a0078442537900ceeb8e83a487aa5f0e71c0.png"]
New baggage exits are now locked while the promotion is missing:

We've repeatedly gotten feedback from you, and also observed it while watching streams, that the state in which you've unlocked a new extension with a new baggage exit is super confusing. That's why the new baggage exit is now locked until you've actually bought the promotion and relevant baggage appears at that exit.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45764717/24f3dfe48c750b9779808289c17234bf0bcdeeb8.png"]

We've been asked fairly often how you actually get decoration points and complete the first quest about it. That's why there's now a new yellow quest marker during this quest that leads you to Deco-Denise, as long as you don't have any decoration points yet.

The quest to reach the promotion to "Master" requires you to send 40 suitcases to "DEL". "DEL", however, is at a gate where flights to "DEL" or "AMS" come in at random. In rare cases (when someone had really bad luck) this led to all other conditions for the Master quest being long since done, while things just wouldn't move forward with the "DEL" suitcases because the wrong ones kept coming in. We've tweaked this a bit: it's now the case that, as long as this quest is active, the chance for "DEL" suitcases is 80% instead of just the usual 50%.

The decoration level in the promotion tab was briefly displayed incorrectly after it increased, this meant the requirement to unlock a promotion was shown as unfulfilled in some cases, even though it was not. This is fixed now.
The weight scanner's beam jittered slightly while walking around. It doesn't anymore.
When you held down the scan key on the weight scanner and the scan was finished, the progress bar and the white box on the label weren't hidden. That's now fixed and feels a bit smoother.

We've reworked a few descriptions: the dispenser now clearly points out that it places suitcases on a table if there's room, and the small corner is now clearly called "Corner (small)" instead of "Turntable", because we kept seeing players overlook that a small corner exists at all.

As of today there's a new channel on our Discord where you can share screenshots of your setups or other moments. I'll be sprinkling these into the news every now and then. Today's comes from MiTuZa from our Discord server, who kicked the whole thing off:
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45764717/bfdefd901dcf747ecdd65dcbf0a93b8513e750a8.png"]With \ you can activate screenshot mode in the game! :)
As always, thank you for all the feedback! We're still hard at work collecting feedback across all channels to give you the best possible experience as quickly as we can. 😎
And always remember, airport operations tolerate no negligence!
Stable regards,
Günther!
Three River Games (3RG)
If you haven't read through the first release news yet and are coming fresh from the demo, you'll find the 1.0 changelog here:
[dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/3887090/view/540010953256731632"]
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45150789/aef6cec0321b4206f6364c163a0a2bbb2b81f9cc.png"]
We've kept gathering your feedback attentively and have the next patch ready for you right away.

Many of you have told us that the constant barking gets annoying the longer you play and the more you've automated. That's why you can now set exactly when the sniffer should bark. The default is the previous behavior, meaning it always barks. But you can also set it to bark only when it finds illegal substances, or to never bark at all. You can adjust this in the first tab (General) of the settings:

Many of you also wished for a way to not have to hold down the run key the whole time. There's now a new option for that in the controls settings as well. Here you can decide whether you want to hold the key to run as before, toggle between running and walking, or simply always run.

Some of you let us know that you don't really like being forced to deal intensively with decoration just to reach decoration level two. That's why we've halved the decoration points you need to advance from level 1 to level 2, meaning you save about 6 plants, or just under $2,000, to clear this hurdle. From level two onward the decoration progression is the same as before; this is only about taking the pain out of the quest flow in Terminal 1.
Building parts now keep their rotation when you pick up several in a row. That way you no longer have to realign every conveyor belt when you want to build a longer straight stretch.
When you threw a parcel containing a building part into a sorter, you received upgrade points for it. That's no longer the case — sorters now only give upgrade points when they process suitcases.

We now also save the speed of suitcases. Previously, if a suitcase happened to be in the air at the exact moment the game was closed and you then loaded again, the suitcase would simply drop to the floor instead of keeping the trajectory it had picked up, for example from a thrower or a player's throw, as you'd expect. This also meant that automations relying heavily on throwers would sometimes throw up a bunch of errors right after a restart.
The hint about free skill points is no longer shown once you've already brought all of your abilities to the highest level.
You can now collect up to $3,000 from Rolf. Previously he couldn't even hand out the maximum amount you could reach with upgrades, because it was capped at $1,000.
It was possible to press the keys for the skill menu and the tablet at the same time and open both — that's no longer possible.
While you have a scanner in your hand, you can no longer interact with the arcade or the TVs in the hallway.
A translation error in the German settings has been fixed.

In some languages — French, for example — the texts for the jokes of the day were so long that they didn't fully fit on the TV. That's now fixed.: If you haven't read through the first release news yet and are coming fresh from the demo, you'll find a more detailed changelog here: https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/3887090/view/540010953256731632
As always, thank you for all the feedback! We're still hard at work collecting feedback across all channels to give you the best possible experience as quickly as we can. 😎
And always remember — airport operations tolerate no negligence!
Stable regards,
Günther!

notes.title: Prices for conveyor belts in the jobs

items.text: In the later game there was a problem with one of the negative effects you have to deal with to balance out the benefits in the jobs.
The conveyor belts with the high railings on the side, so that no suitcases fall off, were supposed to cost 300% more, but that wasn't the case.
That was a bit unfortunate, because it let you bypass the system of benefits and burdens in this specific case. It's now fixed, and the price behaves the way you'd expect.

There's now a subfolder with backups for each creation date of a save game. This lets us cover more cases and, should your progress ever be lost for unexpected reasons such as a power outage, help you out of a tight spot more effectively.

notes.title: Extended logging for problems with invisible objects

items.text: There seems to be a rare case in which, roughly along the line where the wall disappears into the floor when you unlock an expansion (this was reported to us in Hall 1 when unlocking JFK), an invisible object is left behind.
That's a bit annoying, because it means you can't build there.

notes.title: Here's a screenshot from the community showing what we mean

items.text: Since we haven't been able to reproduce this case ourselves so far, we've extended our logging so that the name of the object preventing you from building gets written into the log. We're hoping this will let us solve the problem. So we'd like to ask you: if you run into this problem and unexpectedly see a red outline at this or any other spot, meaning you can't build there, then press the left mouse button once, as if you wanted to build there, and send us a report via the feedback form you can open in-game through the menu.

It could happen that you were left stuck with individual pieces of luggage for Terminal 2 that were impossible to deliver correctly.

notes.title: Here's an example of the case we mean

items.text: You received a suitcase for JFK and it's on its way through your automation, and then, in the meantime, you unlock JFK as a new destination airport. In this specific case, the suitcase that was already on its way to Terminal 2 would suddenly become invalid. The problem was that you couldn't bring the old suitcase to the gate either, because it had been saved on the suitcase that it was destined for Terminal 2.

It was especially confusing that you could, for example, also have a pre-scanned yellow suitcase for JFK in the system, then unlock the new airport and receive a pre-scanned green one — while, following the example above, it wasn't possible to deliver the yellow one correctly.

So it could happen that you were left stuck with suitcases that could only be resolved by discarding them as an error. That's of course not an acceptable state, and it's now fixed with the new version! :)
If you haven't read through the first release news yet and are coming fresh from the demo, you'll find a more detailed changelog here:

Of course, we've been busy gathering your feedback and put together a patch right away.

In the quest line where illegal substances and how to check for them with the sniffer are introduced for the first time, it could happen that it took a very long time for the first suitcase containing illegal substances to appear. We've built in a little shortcut here that makes sure the first suitcase that appears after you've looked at the illegal-substances check on your tablet always contains illegal substances. With this, we hope to catch cases where someone gets stuck on the quests for 15 minutes because the right suitcase just doesn't happen to show up.
Trash lying under the "Joke of the Day" TV in Millhome couldn't be removed as expected because an invisible object was hanging over it.
The "Joke of the Day" wasn't being shuffled properly; it could happen that the same joke was told on two consecutive days.
There was unfortunately a typo in our Czech logo — we've corrected it and swapped it out.

It was possible to interact with the whiteboard while holding the scanner. This led to some players neatly arranging a stack to scan on the table in front of the whiteboard, only to keep losing their flow when trying to scan because the whiteboard interaction unexpectedly triggered instead.

Günther Gewinn here again. As the airport's managing director, it is my honor and my duty to present the changes in version 0.3 of Airport Baggage Simulator!
A new sorter with two outputs: one for suitcases with a valid airline sticker and one for suitcases with an invalid sticker.

notes.title: 🤖 Automation for Baggage Carts and Green Scanner Machine

items.text: An automatic scanner for validating baggage (green) as well as a baggage thrower that can automatically load baggage carts.
A new scanner (yellow) to automate Terminal 2 baggage.
A new check (weight) and a new gate that serves flights to both DEL and AMS can now be unlocked.
New work equipment: A baggage scale that lets you check whether the suitcase's weight has been paid for
Invest skill points in the Backpack to be able to carry more packages or suitcases around at once.
You can unlock two new wall and two new floor decorations from Deco-Denise.
Starting now, you can unlock Jumbo suitcases, which earn you significantly higher income per piece than conventional baggage.

notes.title: 🛫 New Upgrade for the Airport Sorter

items.text: You can now unlock an upgrade for the Airport Sorter that allows you to filter by two destination airports.
We increased the base speed of all conveyor belts and machines. To illustrate, here's a conveyor line with one upgrade each before and after the changes.
Sorting machines now work faster, especially at the beginning of the game.
Straight conveyor belts and large conveyor-belt curves are now 33% faster.
Turntables now rotate within one second instead of 1.5 seconds.
Suitcases now cross bridges within 3.5 instead of 4.5 seconds.
Giving plants love (upgrading them) now also improves their contribution to the decor level.
Plant upgrades now go up to level 7 instead of only up to level 4.
There are two new colors: Pink and Yellow.
The railings of straight conveyor belts and large curves are now colored as well.
It is now possible to color the conveyor belt of the substance sniffer.
For every skill point you invest in Janitor, you will receive +50 XP and +$10 whenever you dispose of trash or mop the floor (two points were invested in the clip below).
Rolf has "recalculated" his payouts once again. We improved his quality upgrade: per upgrade rank, you now get at least $10 more than before. In the image above, the upgrade is at Rank 3.

Package delivery can now be automated: If a conveyor belt is placed on the X on the floor, packages are caught out of the air and placed onto the belt, and Horst waits with the next throw until there's free space. (Previously, the problem was that the packages wouldn't stay on the belt or would knock each other off.)
Packages thrown into a baggage exit are no longer destroyed; instead, they reappear directly above the player's head and fall down.
In languages without latin letters, text that should have been readable on some of the TV screens, was invisible.
The elevated conveyor belt that could be unlocked through an upgrade at the dog was often the reason suitcases got stuck on what seemed like a straight conveyor-belt section.
It was possible to rotate the camera view while the feedback form was open.
Sometimes Rolf would examine suitcases in his absence and grant extra money.
It was possible to draw on whiteboards while the menu was open.
It is no longer possible to accidentally draw on whiteboards while holding the mouse button and walking by, for example while carrying baggage.
It could happen that the quest to find illegal substances with the sniffer could not be completed if the automation for the dog was unlocked beforehand.
After closing the feedback form the game was in a bugged state until the menu was opened and closed again.
It is no longer possible to build an endless UP farm. A machine now only grants UP progress once per suitcase, not over and over again.
Scanning a baggage item no longer grants XP multiple times.
Flipped conveyor belts no longer reverse direction after being upgraded.
Fixed city name labels overflowing on the Terminal 2 receiver in languages with longer names (e.g., Portuguese).
Fixed baggage occasionally not being picked up by storage.
To better distinguish packed building parts, there is now a hint showing the part's name while you carry it around in a package.
When you look at a sorter or any other building part that isn't a conveyor belt, a hint with the part's name is now displayed as well.
When suitcases are placed onto a table by a machine, the tag is now automatically rotated to match the table's orientation.
The default mouse speed has been reduced by 40%.
You can now use the mouse wheel to rotate buildings while placing them.
Suitcases can now be rotated both with the R key and with C.
It is now possible to interact with doors when you carry parcels or baggage.
XP & UP popups have subtler sounds, better-formatted text, and a subtler presentation when many popups appear within a short time or at a large distance from the player.
Build quests now include explained quest steps for clearer guidance.
The plant "Rüdiger" has been improved and now provides 10 XP instead of 1 XP per upgrade level every 60 seconds.
Another plant "Kevin" that gives you a money bonus can now be bought after being promoted to trainee.
The number of invalid suitcases per flight is no longer always one, but now varies randomly to make things more interesting.
Additional suitcases now arrive between flights: starting at one every 15 seconds. The interval between suitcases decreases by 3 seconds for each promotion you've unlocked.
The trash can has been given a fresh coat of paint and now indicates that you get money back for disposing of packages.
Removing columns is much cheaper at the beginning and gets more expensive the farther back the column is in the hall.
For every skill point invested in Merchant you now get back 6% of the money instead of 2%.
For every skill point invested in Technician you now get reduce the price of upgrades by 8% instead of 4%.
The cost of the second upgrade of all sorter machines was reduced by $200.
Deko-Denise's email now points out that plants can be improved.
We have reduced the amount of upgrades for conveyors from 5 to 3, but increased the speed boost each individual upgrade unlocks.
The joke of the day has been added in Japanese with voice acting.
When a machine's output ends on a table, suitcases are rotated so that their front faces the front of the table, making them as easy as possible to process further.
New quest for substance sniffer automation, helping players discover this feature more reliably.

Airport Baggage Simulator now has, in addition to English, its own logo and title translation in the following languages: German, Japanese, French, Brazilian Portuguese, Simplified Chinese, Polish, Czech, Russian, Spanish, and Italian.
Special thanks to Rusty Champaign, the YouTuber with the most-viewed video about the 0.2 update. To honor that, we added Champaign (CMI) as a new destination airport for Terminal 2.
We hope you enjoy the new version! If you do, be sure to add the game to your wishlist so you don't miss future updates.
And always remember – airport operations tolerate no negligence!
Solid greetings,
Günther!

items.text: This is Günther Gewinn speaking. Thank you for your positive and numerous reactions to Version 0.2! We have been carefully gathering feedback and decided to roll out one more update before Christmas!

To make getting started with automation easier and more interesting, we have reduced the cost of upgrades and significantly increased the speed at which UP is earned in the beginning. Additionally, storage is now more affordable.
The first 36 UP points are now easier to earn
UP costs for machine upgrades have been reduced (halved for upgrades 2 and 3)
Price for storage reduced from 650 to 350
We have added a new machine: The Dispenser. This machine places items onto workbenches in a controlled manner.
We have adjusted the orientation of suitcases as they exit machines to allow for a smoother workflow.
Baggage is now rotated by default when leaving machines so that the tag points 90 degrees to the right, which in most cases means it faces the player
Exception: At the red exit of the Lost & Found machine, the rotation was deliberately inverted because it is more practical for the common setup at the start of the game (see below)
Minor adjustments to the gameplay and user interface.
The game now pauses completely while the pause menu is open
New Demo Key Art integrated into the start screen
Additional tips added to the pause menu, e.g., recommending the use of a distributor to balance the load and generate more UP.
Solid regards,
Günther!
Three River Games (3RG)
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45150789/aef6cec0321b4206f6364c163a0a2bbb2b81f9cc.png"]
This is Günther Gewinn speaking again. It is my honor and my duty as the airport’s managing director to present the changes in version 0.2 of Airport Baggage Simulator!
We’ve given the machines a fresh coat of paint and added several new ones to automate tasks such as load balancing, baggage sorting, and scanning.
New sorters for baggage type, label color, destination airport, and illegal substances
Load balancing with splitter and merger machines for parallel conveyor belts
Machines now show a status light and progress bars on multiple sides while working
Machine speed can now be upgraded
We improved the build preview for machines
There are now machines that let you automate baggage scanning
We’ve replaced the bridge and the 1m curve with sturdier variants. In addition, we added a taller bridge variant as well as a larger 2m radius curve.
Bridge and 1m curve replaced with sturdier versions (suitcases get stuck or roll off less often)
New taller bridge variant you can walk underneath
New 2m radius curve for more varied designs
Conveyor belts can now be colored
We fixed conveyor belts running slower on high-end PCs with unlimited FPS (they are now FPS-independent and always run at the same speed)
The substance sniffer can now be integrated into the automation system and has a new resting spot, plus a few small interactions.
Baggage is now marked with red or green paw stickers while being sniffed, indicating whether a substance is inside
A separate machine can then sort incoming baggage by these paw stickers
Automation upgrade enables direct connection to conveyor belts
You can now pet the dog
The dog bowl can now be refilled once per day
The doghouse is gone; instead there’s a nice big mat so you can see and pet the good boy from all sides

We’ve given Rolf a selection of general improvements with the goal of enabling automation of suitcase hand-ins to Rolf and ensuring that money earned from substance suitcases remains meaningful later in the game.
New upgrade system with speed, quality (shows payout range), and daily capacity upgrades
Rolf now also appears on Tuesdays
Rolf now has a daily limit of baggage he can process (upgradeable)
Room connection between delivery room and main hall unlockable via upgrade
Rolf keeps working and collects money from multiple suitcases when you present him with a stack of baggage
We’ve introduced gates with animated baggage carts and rolling doors, as well as new baggage exits for the different controls. The goal is to create a stronger sense of real airport work.
New gates with animated rolling doors and baggage carts driven into the hall by airport staff
View of the outside area with runway and more airport atmosphere
Incoming baggage now always belongs to a specific flight at a gate and no longer appears endlessly on the conveyor belt
Each invalid baggage type—i.e., each control you use to sort out baggage—now has its own exit from the terminal
Each flight has a scheduled time; at that time the baggage cart departs automatically
“Last flight of the day” system ensures you can finish the remaining work before the day ends
Gates can be upgraded to receive more baggage per flight
We’ve introduced a new upgrade system. Running machines generate Upgrade Points (UP), which you can spend on these upgrades.
New upgrade system for machines, conveyor belts, upgrades at Rolf, and some environment objects (for example, remove the pillars in the center of the room via an upgrade to gain more space)
New currency: Upgrade Points (UP), generated by running machines
Upgrade UI shows available upgrades when you look at upgradeable objects
You can visit Denise, the decoration lady, to buy plants, wall textures, and floorings. Decoration not only gives the terminal a fresh look, but also provides progression.
New decoration room with Denise, comes with the third room expansion
Denise sells plants, wall textures, and floorings
The more decoration you place, the higher your “Deco Level” becomes. Each Deco Level increases your income by 5%
Different plants also grant XP, UP, and money bonuses (1-minute cooldown)
Plants can be improved with upgrades
We added new skills. Also, there is now a bouncing arrow and a friendly sound when you level up.
New skill: UP bonus
New skill: Reduced upgrade costs
New skill: Refund on shop deliveries
Bouncing arrow in the skill panel indicates available skill points
XP is now granted immediately upon confirming a delivery, not only after the cart departs

We focused on automation stability and fixed many issues where baggage got stuck, was lost, or blocked machines. You can now also throw baggage and packages, and there are a few improvements to make handling baggage easier!
You can now throw baggage and packages
Baggage snaps into free slots in the baggage cart
Baggage rotates in the expected direction when leaving machines
Numerous edge cases with triggers, deactivation, and baggage getting stuck between machines fixed
Issues with baggage spawning and persistence after loading save games fixed
Once you’ve completed the work instruction, you can now freely move your workbenches! We also added placement validation and worked to make building feel better overall.
Workbenches can be moved once the work instruction is completed
Validation prevents placement in invalid positions
Preview is now visible when looking straight ahead and snaps to the grid at maximum distance
Direction arrows for corners and other direction-dependent buildings
Green and red scanner tables are now two separate objects
Scanner tables snap correctly to the grid and can be cleanly placed against walls
Green scanner table displays valid destination airports on a screen
Various edge cases with outlines, upgrades, and controls fixed

We redesigned the UI and added full controller support. There’s also a streamlined tutorial and, fitting with promotions that unlock new things, you now have milestone quests. In addition to many other small improvements, we also added a screenshot mode.
The game is now fully playable with a controller
UI redesign with improved colors, fonts, layout, and overlay canvas
Screenshot mode added (usable with )
New milestone quests with multiple objectives
Streamlined tutorial with better pacing and fewer interruptions
Shop UI reorganized with tabs and newly arranged items in the order they are unlocked
Additional music tracks added that you can switch between on the radio
20 voice-acted “jokes of the day” in German, English, and French
Rolf, Horst, and Denise are temporarily wearing festive Christmas hats
In the pause menu you can now read useful gameplay tips

We added a Twitch integration for streamers. With the chat command “!baggage,” chatters can register their names on incoming baggage, and with “!jump” they can make their baggage jump for entertainment—without significantly disrupting the streamer’s gameplay.
Twitch chat usernames are displayed on baggage
Chat can make its baggage jump
Streamer mode and individual Twitch integration features can be enabled or disabled in the settings
We added a mop to loosen up the core gameplay a bit and give you a nice way to earn extra XP.
You can pick up the mop at one of the two cleaning stations and wipe away dirt in the terminal
Cleaning grants a considerable amount of XP
More dirt appears depending on your expansion progress

We made many small changes to the environment and collision physics so things look better and are less annoying while walking around and handling suitcases. We also distributed collectible trash throughout the entire terminal for variety and as another small source of XP and money.
Collectible trash distributed throughout the entire terminal (one-time cleanup rewards)
Improved colliders throughout the terminal to prevent baggage from getting stuck or lost
A total of four room expansions to unlock in the demo
Various visual fixes to walls, room connections, and other objects
We added whiteboards where you can doodle and get creative.
Whiteboards placed near Lost & Found and in the hallway

You can draw with a black marker and also clean the whiteboard again: (If you’ve created a particularly nice masterpiece, feel free to take a picture of it (Screenshot mode with F6!) and share it on Discord. When you close the game, your artworks will be wiped away by the cleaning staff—so immortalize them beforehand! :D)
We made many small improvements.
Hand scanner range increased from two to four meters
Doors now always open away from you
Shifts can be paused and resumed. While paused, no new flights arrive or depart and time stands still
A yellow marker reminds you at 9:00 AM to start your shift
Money popups now only appear for manual deliveries, not automated ones, to reduce UI clutter (you still get the money, of course)
TVs above invalid baggage conveyor belts display simplified content from a distance for better readability
Ambient sounds and UI sounds have been revised in many places
We hope you enjoy the new version! If you do, be sure to add the game to your wishlist so you don’t miss further updates!
You also still have a chance to secure a spot in the Closed Beta Playtest for the full version! To do so, play the demo and then fill out this short survey.
